entries.title: Take the document from where it arrives
entries.does: Captures a document as bytes wherever it lands, without a second request of our own.
entries.when: The page opens a PDF in a new window, streams it to an in-page viewer, or delivers it with no plain link.
steps: Listen for responses whose type is a PDF across the page and any popup or new window, including bytes carried as base64 inside a JSON reply.
When a download event fires, read the download to bytes rather than relying on a saved file path.
When an in-page viewer consumes the stream so the bytes are no longer readable, re-read the same already-issued request and keep its body before handing it on.
Confirm the bytes begin with the PDF marker before treating the capture as a document.
entries.limits: Fails when the document is never a real file, only pixels drawn on screen, which needs render-to-PDF instead.

entries.title: Fetch the document by its own URL with the session
entries.does: Reads the document with a plain GET that carries the signed-in session.
entries.when: The document has a stable link and the session is held in cookies.
steps: Read the link target from the rendered control.
Resolve a relative target against the current page address.
GET that address with the live session and an Accept header for PDF.
Confirm the reply begins with the PDF marker before accepting it.
entries.limits: Fails when the link carries a single-use token that is already spent, or the document needs a session the GET does not carry.

entries.title: Render an HTML-only document to PDF
entries.does: Produces a PDF from a document that the portal only ever draws as a web page.
entries.when: A statement or notice is shown as HTML and no PDF is offered.
steps: Open the document view and wait until it is fully rendered.
Use the browser's own print-to-PDF to capture the rendered page.
Keep the resulting bytes as the document.
entries.limits: Loses fidelity when the page depends on screen-only layout, and cannot capture content behind a control the page never expands.

entries.title: Read the document list from the data behind the page
entries.does: Lists documents from the read-only data feed the page itself reads, then fetches each one.
entries.when: The page is drawn by its own script from a data feed and the on-screen list is awkward to read.
steps: Find the read endpoint the page uses to list documents and GET it with the live session.
Take each document's own date and identity from that data, not from on-screen order.
GET each document by the address the data gives.
entries.limits: Fails when the feed needs a token the session cannot replay, or reports a document exists when its content is not yet ready.

entries.title: Expand an archive of documents
entries.does: Turns a single archive download into one document per file inside it.
entries.when: The portal hands back several statements bundled in one archive.
steps: Capture the archive as bytes.
Expand it in memory.
Treat each inner PDF as its own document.
entries.limits: Fails when the archive is encrypted or holds formats other than the documents expected.

entries.title: Resume a large download by byte range
entries.does: Retries only the missing part of a large download instead of starting over.
entries.when: A large document download fails partway on a slow or unreliable link.
steps: Track how many bytes have arrived.
On a break, GET the same document again asking only for the bytes still missing.
Join the parts and confirm the whole is a valid document.
entries.limits: Fails when the source does not honor ranged requests or the content changes between attempts.

entries.title: Name the file by the date inside the document
entries.does: Labels a document by the statement date printed inside it, not the row it came from.
entries.when: The list date may be a posting or availability date that differs from the period the document covers.
steps: Read the statement date from the first page of the captured document, or from an authoritative date the data gives.
Prefer that date over the on-screen row date when they disagree.
Name and file the document by that date.
entries.limits: Fails when the document carries no readable date and the data gives none.

entries.title: Enumerate every sub-account by a stable identity key
entries.does: Finds every account under one sign-in and keys each by a durable identity, not a session token.
entries.when: One sign-in sees several accounts and later steps must refer back to a specific one.
steps: List every account the sign-in can reach.
Key each account by a stable identity, such as the last four digits plus the account kind.
Carry that key, never a per-session token, into later steps.
entries.limits: Fails when two accounts share the same visible identity and nothing else tells them apart.

entries.title: Choose the account by identity, else fail loudly
entries.does: Picks the intended account from several by a supplied identity, and stops rather than guess.
entries.when: Several account tiles are shown and only one is the target.
steps: Match the account named in the request first.
If none is named, match a distinguishing pattern for the intended account.
If exactly one account is present, use it.
Otherwise raise a clear error; never take whichever tile is first.
entries.limits: Fails when the request gives no identity and more than one account could match.

entries.title: Switch organization or account when one sign-in sees many
entries.does: Moves to the right organization or account owner before reading its documents.
entries.when: One sign-in spans several organizations or billing owners.
steps: Open the switcher.
Choose the target by its name, not its position.
Confirm the chosen context is active before continuing.
entries.limits: Fails when the switch needs a separate grant the sign-in does not hold.

entries.title: Scout the real document dates before requesting
entries.does: Learns which periods actually have documents, then requests only those.
entries.when: The portal may not have a document for every recent period.
steps: Read the list of periods the portal offers.
Keep only the periods that actually hold a document.
Request those periods rather than a fixed recent-months window.
entries.limits: Fails when the portal hides periods until a control is driven to reveal them.

entries.title: Enter text key by key, not in one shot
entries.does: Types each character into a field so fields that cap or drop pasted input still receive it.
entries.when: A field caps length, trims input, or ignores a single bulk set.
steps: Focus the field.
Type the value one character at a time with a small human-like gap.
Read the field back and confirm it holds the whole value before moving on.
entries.limits: Fails when a floating label or overlay intercepts focus so the field never receives the keys.

entries.title: Wait until the field is editable before typing
entries.does: Waits for inputs and buttons that ship disabled until the page's own script wakes them.
entries.when: A server-drawn form arrives with its fields or submit disabled until it hydrates.
steps: Wait for the field and its submit control to become enabled.
Only then enter text and submit.
Treat a control that stays disabled past the budget as a terminal failure.
entries.limits: Fails when the control never enables because an earlier step the page expects was skipped.

entries.title: Click the named control by its accessible name
entries.does: Clicks a control by its role and exact accessible name, skipping decoys.
entries.when: The page has look-alike controls such as locale pickers or third-party sign-in buttons.
steps: Find the control by its role and exact accessible name.
Confirm it is the visible, intended control before clicking.
Click it, letting the match reach controls inside open shadow roots.
entries.limits: Fails when the real control carries no accessible name or shares its name with a decoy.

entries.title: Handle one-step and two-step sign-in
entries.does: Fills the identifier, then adapts to whatever the portal shows next.
entries.when: The portal may ask for the password on the same screen or on a second one.
steps: Enter the identifier.
If a password field is already present, use it.
Otherwise advance and wait for whichever comes first: a password field, a one-time code prompt, or an already-signed-in area.
Continue down the branch that actually appeared.
entries.limits: Fails when the next screen is a challenge the session cannot satisfy.

entries.title: Handle the returning-user layout
entries.does: Signs in on the visible password field when the identifier is already remembered.
entries.when: A remembered profile hides or prefills the identifier and shows only a password prompt.
steps: Treat the identifier as optional when it is already filled.
Enter the password on the visible password field.
Submit once and prove the outcome.
entries.limits: Fails when the remembered profile belongs to the wrong account.

entries.title: Start from the flow that leads to the documents
entries.does: Begins at the sign-in that actually reaches the work, not a marketing page.
entries.when: The portal has several entry points and only one leads to the needed area.
steps: Point the start address at the flow that leads to the target area.
Avoid bare marketing or generic landing pages.
Confirm the signed-in area is the one that holds the documents.
entries.limits: Fails when the direct flow is itself gated by a step only the generic entry sets up.

entries.title: Prove sign-in positively, not by leaving the login screen
entries.does: Trusts sign-in only on a positive, stable signal of the signed-in area.
entries.when: Deciding whether sign-in actually succeeded.
steps: Require a known signed-in signal, such as the expected area's address or an element only present once inside.
Require that signal to hold stable across repeated checks.
Never treat merely leaving the login screen as success.
entries.limits: Fails when the signed-in signal is also shown briefly during an interstitial.

entries.title: A block disguised as an outage is terminal
entries.does: Recognizes a portal-unavailable message held across checks and stops.
entries.when: The portal shows an outage-worded page that may be a standing refusal.
steps: Match known portal-unavailable wording.
Require it to persist across several consecutive checks.
Raise a terminal unavailable error rather than retrying for minutes.
entries.limits: A genuine brief outage is reported the same way and will be given up on.

entries.title: Bound retries on an ambiguous rejection
entries.does: Retries a vaguely worded rejection a few times on fresh sessions, then reports it honestly.
entries.when: The portal says something generic like your details did not match, which may be a soft block.
steps: Treat an ambiguous rejection as possibly a soft block, not certainly wrong credentials.
Retry on a fresh session, at most a small fixed number of times.
Then report an ambiguous rejection, not a flat claim that the password is wrong.
entries.limits: Retrying real wrong credentials still burns attempts and can harden a block.

entries.title: Request a one-time code and wait for it within a budget
entries.does: Raises a code challenge and waits for a person to supply the code, bounded in rounds and time.
entries.when: Sign-in, or a step-up inside the work area, demands a one-time code only a person can read.
steps: Record that a code is needed and wait for it to be supplied through the agreed hand-off.
Poll for the supplied code within a fixed time budget.
Cap the number of challenge rounds.
Keep the person's wait outside any per-item time limit so a single item's budget cannot cancel it.
entries.limits: Fails when no person answers inside the budget.

entries.title: Confirm the code was actually sent, and pick the channel deliberately
entries.does: Chooses the delivery channel by name and requires proof the code was sent before waiting.
entries.when: The portal offers a choice of where to send the code and may silently not send.
steps: Choose the delivery channel by its accessible name, in a deliberate order, polling for buttons that appear late.
Trigger the send.
Require the portal's own acknowledgement, or the rendered code field, before raising the challenge.
If no acknowledgement comes, retry the send a few times or try another offered channel, then fail clearly.
entries.limits: Fails when the portal acknowledges a send it did not actually deliver.

entries.title: Confirm the submit took, and never ask for a second code
entries.does: Verifies the code form actually advanced, reading a silent rejection from the form staying put, without ever requesting another code.
entries.when: Submitting a one-time code, where a click may do nothing and a rejection may be silent.
steps: Do not trigger another send when the code form is already showing.
Submit the code once and wait for the code form to detach before deciding anything.
Treat the form still being present as a silent rejection, not a prompt to resend.
Never request a second code; hand back when the first is not accepted.
entries.limits: Fails when the portal keeps the form visible briefly even after accepting the code.

entries.title: Keep device trust so later sessions skip the code
entries.does: Accepts a remember-this-device offer so the trust is kept in the session's own profile.
entries.when: The portal offers to trust the device and a persistent profile is in use.
steps: Tick the remember or trust option when offered.
Let the trust land in the persistent profile.
Reuse that profile on later runs so one code can cover many sessions.
entries.limits: Fails on portals that grant no durable trust or whose sessions are always fresh.

entries.title: Switch to an offered alternate code method
entries.does: Moves to an offered code method the session can satisfy when the default one it cannot.
entries.when: The default factor is something the session cannot answer but another offered method it can.
steps: Open the method picker when the default factor cannot be answered.
Choose an offered method that the session can satisfy.
Continue the code flow on that method.
entries.limits: Fails when no satisfiable method is offered.

entries.title: Never wait for network idle
entries.does: Judges readiness by settling signals rather than by the network going quiet.
entries.when: Any page whose own script keeps sending background traffic.
steps: Use a settle check or an address-stable check instead of waiting for network idle.
Treat a page that streams telemetry as normal, not as never-ready.
entries.limits: A settle check can still fire early on a page that pauses mid-render.

entries.title: Poll for the real content, not the URL or load event
entries.does: Waits for the actual rows, tiles or links to appear, within a budget.
entries.when: Content is drawn by the page's own script after the load event.
steps: Decide which real element proves the content arrived.
Poll for that element within a time budget.
Do not judge content absent at the load event or from the address alone.
entries.limits: Fails when the proof element never appears because an earlier step did not take.

entries.title: Read the link target and navigate, instead of clicking
entries.does: Follows a control's own link with a GET when a click cannot land.
entries.when: Overlays intercept clicks, a submenu is collapsed, or a custom control ignores clicks.
steps: Read the link target from the control.
Navigate to that target directly.
Confirm the expected content arrived.
entries.limits: Fails when the control has no readable target and acts only through its own handler.

entries.title: See content inside shadow roots via the accessibility tree
entries.does: Reaches rows drawn inside shadow roots through the role and accessibility view.
entries.when: Rows are rendered inside shadow roots and are invisible to a plain element search.
steps: Use the role and accessibility view, which crosses open shadow roots, to find the content.
Target each item by its role and name.
Confirm the item is visible before acting on it.
entries.limits: Fails when the content sits in a closed shadow root the accessibility view cannot reach.

entries.title: Drive accordions, pickers, pagination and generators
entries.does: Operates the controls that load more rows, checking each action took effect.
entries.when: Rows appear only after driving a dropdown, accordion, date picker, generate button or pager.
steps: Identify the control that loads the rows.
Drive it and confirm the picked value or page actually changed.
Read the rows that appear, then repeat for the next page or period.
entries.limits: Fails when a control silently refuses and shows no change to detect.

entries.title: Adopt new tabs, popups and cross-origin hand-offs
entries.does: Follows the work when it opens in a new tab, popup or a hand-off to another origin.
entries.when: A click opens content in a new window or routes through a separate sign-in origin.
steps: Expect a new page when a control may open one.
Adopt the new page and continue the work there.
Follow a cross-origin hand-off back to where the content lands.
entries.limits: Fails when the new page is blocked before it opens, or the hand-off never returns.

entries.title: Bound every per-item loop with a time limit
entries.does: Wraps each account, loan or period in its own time limit and isolates its failure.
entries.when: Looping over many items where one stuck item could hang the whole run.
steps: Give each item its own time limit.
Fail that item alone when the limit is reached.
Carry on with the remaining items.
entries.limits: A dropped browser connection can keep built-in timeouts from firing, so the per-item limit must be enforced by us.

entries.title: Target the visible control, never the first match
entries.does: Binds a control to the visible one among several matches, not the first in document order.
entries.when: A page holds hidden mirrors or decoys that share a control's description.
steps: Gather the candidates by role and accessible name.
Keep only the ones that are actually visible.
Act on the intended visible control, never on whichever is first.
entries.limits: Fails when more than one visible control matches and nothing else distinguishes them.

entries.title: Resolve the right frame by its URL
entries.does: Finds the login or content frame by matching its own address, not a racy frame lookup.
entries.when: The real work sits in a frame that is lazy, often unnamed, and wrapped by chrome-only frames.
steps: Poll the page's frames for the one whose address matches the target.
Make sure the pattern does not also match the outer wrapper.
Work inside that frame once it is present.
entries.limits: Fails when the frame's address is generic enough to match the wrapper too.

entries.title: Clear splashes, cookie walls and promos; never consent or enroll for the user
entries.does: Dismisses blocking splashes, cookie walls and promo takeovers while declining to opt in on the user's behalf.
entries.when: A splash, disclaimer, cookie wall or promo covers the page before or during the work.
steps: Dismiss known splashes, disclaimers, cookie walls and promo takeovers, keeping a registry of the ones seen.
Tick only consent that is strictly required to proceed.
Never enroll in anything or grant optional consent without an explicit go-ahead.
entries.limits: Fails when a new interstitial not yet in the registry blocks the page.

entries.title: Navigate by the live href; capture tokens before they vanish
entries.does: Moves through the portal using its live links and grabs per-account tokens before the page drops them.
entries.when: Links and lists carry single-use session tokens that do not survive a cold reload.
steps: Read the live link target, which carries the session token, instead of building or guessing an address.
Capture per-account tokens before they disappear from view.
Reopen the list and re-scan it after each document, keyed on the list's links being present rather than on the address.
Move within the app rather than reloading cold.
entries.limits: Fails when the token is bound so tightly to one view that reopening the list reissues it.

entries.title: Use the account's persistent profile as the session
entries.does: Treats the account's stored browser profile as the primary session, with cookies only as a fallback.
entries.when: A session should carry across runs and keep device trust.
steps: Run with the account's own persistent profile.
Use stored cookies only as a fallback.
Never let a cookie fallback overwrite a good profile.
entries.limits: Fails when the portal issues only short-lived, non-reusable sessions.

entries.title: Move the profile aside to force a fresh flow
entries.does: Sets the stored profile aside so the next run goes through the full sign-in again.
entries.when: A trusted profile skips pickers or steps that need to be seen or re-exercised.
steps: Rename the account's profile aside, keeping it so the change can be undone.
Run once so a fresh sign-in and its full set of pickers appear.
Restore the profile afterward if the old session is still wanted.
entries.limits: Forces a new code prompt, so it costs a round-trip with a person.

entries.title: Guard against money actions with a request and control block
entries.does: Blocks state-changing requests and refuses payment-like controls so a read-only session cannot move money.
entries.when: Always, on a session that is meant to read and never transact.
steps: Before sign-in, arm a guard that aborts any state-changing request matching payment patterns.
Refuse to click controls whose names match payment or transfer actions, raising a blocked-action error.
Let the guard trip propagate rather than being swallowed.
entries.limits: Pattern-based guards can miss an unusually named money action, so they are a backstop, not the only control.

entries.title: Build targets from the live screen, not from guesses
entries.does: Derives targets by scouting the live screen across every frame, visible and hidden, rather than guessing.
entries.when: Before writing or repairing a driver for an unfamiliar screen.
steps: Scout the live screen and list its inputs and controls across every frame.
Build targets from what is actually present, by role and name.
Do not rely on guessed descriptions.
entries.limits: A scout captures one moment, so a screen that changes shape per visit still needs re-scouting.

entries.title: Capture masked evidence on every failure
entries.does: Saves a screenshot, address and page text for each failure, masked and protected off development.
entries.when: A job fails and the cause must be diagnosable later.
steps: On failure, capture a screenshot, the address and the page text.
Mask and protect the capture outside development.
Keep plain captures only in development.
entries.limits: A capture taken after the page has moved on can miss the moment of failure.

entries.title: Prove the pipeline end to end on a controllable fake portal
entries.does: Runs the whole pipeline against a controllable fake portal and asserts on real delivered bytes.
entries.when: Proving the pipeline works without touching a real institution.
steps: Serve a fake portal with sign-in, a one-time code, a document list and a document.
Run the real pipeline against it end to end, resolving the fake portal only in a demo mode that fails closed.
Clear state first and assert on the bytes that actually came through, not on a completed flag.
entries.limits: A fake portal only exercises the hazards it was built to model.

entries.title: Classify a failure before repairing it
entries.does: Sorts a failure into reseed, wall or drift, and only drift calls for a driver repair.
entries.when: A job has failed and the next action must be chosen.
steps: Call it reseed when credentials are rejected in a real browser.
Call it a wall when a block or unavailable signature appears.
Call it drift when it failed only after reaching navigation, the list or the download.
Trigger a repair for drift alone.
entries.limits: A failure that looks like drift but is really an intermittent wall will send work to repair needlessly.

entries.title: Pace attempts and cap them hard
entries.does: Enforces a gap between sign-in attempts, hard caps, cooldowns and a ledger that fails closed.
entries.when: Any portal where repeated attempts risk a lockout or a block.
steps: Require a minimum gap between sign-in attempts.
Cap session attempts and ambiguous attempts to a small fixed number.
Keep a per-portal, per-account attempt ledger that fails closed when its state is unknown.
Apply per-portal cooldowns after trouble.
entries.limits: A ledger that cannot read its own state must refuse, which can stall a healthy account.

entries.title: After the password is submitted, treat failures as terminal
entries.does: Once the password is sent, stops rather than blindly resubmitting.
entries.when: A failure happens after the password has already been submitted.
steps: Mark the moment the password is submitted.
After that, treat every failure as terminal, except an ambiguous rejection still shown on the form.
Never blindly resubmit, which could fire another code or lock the account.
entries.limits: A genuine transient failure after submit is given up on rather than retried.

entries.title: Scout a live portal with a single-attempt driver
entries.does: Explores a live portal once per run instead of bursting many attempts.
entries.when: Scouting a live portal that throttles or blocks on repeated attempts.
steps: Scout with a driver that makes a single attempt.
Avoid harnesses that burst several session attempts in a row.
Space any further look behind the attempt caps.
entries.limits: A single attempt gives less coverage per run than a burst would.
